summary: Sweep the undeclared-status invariant across the four services TKT-256 did not examine
description:
**Filed 2026-08-25 by a backlog review. TKT-256's own AC asked for this and it was neither done nor split out.**

TKT-256 declared the 500 that `GET /internal/operations` can already answer in payments. Its description said plainly:

> **Worth checking while here:** whether OTHER operations in the payments contract (and the other services' contracts) have the same shape — a handler that can write a status the spec does not declare.

and its closeout recorded:

> Deliberately out of scope: whether catalog / commerce / inventory / access have the same shape is **unexamined**. … **If you want it, it is a new ticket — flagged, not silently dropped.**

This is that ticket. Under ADR-028 the services fail closed and validate responses against the spec, so an **undeclared status is itself a contract violation** — the caller gets a generic 500 saying "response violates OpenAPI contract" instead of the status the handler meant, and the real cause is obscured exactly when someone is debugging an outage.

**A first pass was run while filing, and it changes the expected shape of the work.** Do not treat these as findings to fix — treat them as evidence about what the sweep must be able to see:

- A naive "does the operation declare 500?" scan flags four operations, and **three of them are correct**: `getOrder` and `getDeliveryEmail` (commerce) declare **503**, which is what `persistenceReadProblem` (`services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:1354-1359`) actually returns; `getOpenAPISpec` (catalog) serves a static byte string and has no error path.
- The one real finding is different in kind from what was expected. `holdSeating` (`services/inventory/internal/api/seating.go:28-31`) maps **every** `ClaimIsSeated` error to **404 "not found"** — so a database fault is reported to an internal caller as a missing hold. It declares no 500 and cannot emit one; the defect is that it *swallows* the fault rather than that it undeclares it.

**So the invariant to build is "every status a handler can write is declared", not "every operation declares 500."** A status-name checklist would have passed all four of the above and found nothing.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Establish, per service, the set of statuses each handler can actually write, and diff it against the declared set. State the method and its blind spots — a purely spec-side scan cannot see handler behaviour, which is the same constraint TKT-178 hit for 404s.
- [ ] Every genuine mismatch is either fixed (declare it) or recorded with a reason.
- [ ] `holdSeating`'s error collapse is decided: distinguish a store fault from a missing hold, or record why 404-for-everything is right on an internal route.
- [ ] The mutation that is evidence: remove one declaration and the new check goes red. A check that stays green with a declaration deleted is measuring the spec against itself.

**Non-goals:** changing any handler's chosen status (except `holdSeating`, above); the catalog 404 sweep (TKT-178); re-doing TKT-142's 400 invariant, which is the template.

Quality gates: `make check`; regenerated `openapi_gen.go` / `api-types.gen.ts` committed **before** the gate runs (AGENTS.md).

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Filed by the 2026-08-25 backlog review. TKT-256 asked for this check in its own description, scoped it out to keep the diff small, and its closeout says *"If you want it, it is a new ticket — flagged, not silently dropped."* Nobody filed it.

**A first pass was run before filing, and it is the reason this ticket is worth reading rather than assuming.** The obvious framing — "find operations missing a 500" — produces four hits of which **three are false positives** (two correctly declare 503; one is a static document with no error path). The single real finding is `holdSeating` collapsing every store error into 404, which that framing would have missed entirely.

That is recorded in the description so shaping does not re-derive it, and so the ticket is not planned against a predicate that cannot see the defect (AGENTS.md: a harness that cannot catch what it hunts).

**Needs shaping before Gate 1.**

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Strongest unshaped candidate — no product decision, and the hard part is already done

Backlog review 2026-08-26 at HEAD `1aaee7cd`. Still unshaped (no `readiness`); this comment records why it should be shaped next.

**Nothing has delivered it** — TKT-256 closed payments only, and its closeout says the other four services are unexamined.

**Why this is the best of the remaining unshaped tickets.** The expensive, error-prone part — working out a predicate that can actually see the defect — was done at filing and recorded in the description: a naive "does the operation declare 500?" scan yields four hits of which **three are false positives** (`getOrder` and `getDeliveryEmail` correctly declare 503; `getOpenAPISpec` serves a static byte string with no error path), and the one real finding (`holdSeating` collapsing every store error into 404) is a shape that framing would miss entirely. That is exactly the AGENTS.md trap about a harness that cannot catch what it hunts, pre-cleared.

**TKT-178 has since shipped a working template for the mechanism.** Its `TestCatalogStoreErrorOperationsDeclareNotFound` discovers operations from the Go call graph and checks the document rather than deriving from it, with four guards keeping discovery honest. That is the shape a cross-service sweep wants, and it is on `main` to copy. Note TKT-178's recorded residual: a name-based AST graph misses indirect dispatch (method values, interface-held methods). Inherit the limitation knowingly rather than rediscovering it.

**Shaping should establish:** whether the deliverable is per-service invariant tests or one shared one; and, per AGENTS.md, the mutation that is evidence must be one **only the new tier can catch** — a mutation killed by an existing per-service suite proves nothing about the sweep.

**Likely not `risk:low`:** it spans four services' contracts, and any declaration added is a contract change requiring regen committed before the gate.
